issue: Feature flag state-changing endpoints (POST /:name/state and POST /:name/traffic) lack authentication and authorization middleware
evidence: router.route('/:name/state').post(setFeatureState) — no protect/admin middleware applied, unlike all other write endpoints in the project
recommendation: Add protect and admin middleware: router.route('/:name/state').post(protect, admin, setFeatureState) and same for /:name/traffic. Any unauthenticated user can currently enable/disable feature flags.

issue: Autopilot proxy endpoint POST /api/autopilot/feature-control has no authentication middleware
evidence: router.post('/feature-control', asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {... — comment says 'should be admin in production' but protect/admin middleware is not applied
recommendation: Add protect and admin middleware to the route: router.post('/feature-control', protect, admin, asyncHandler(...)). The comment explicitly acknowledges this gap.

issue: getOrderById does not verify that the requesting user owns the order — any authenticated user can view any order by ID (IDOR)
evidence: const order = await Order.findById(req.params.id).populate('user','name email'); if (order) { res.json(order) } — no check that order.user._id equals req.user._id
recommendation: Add ownership check after fetching: if (order.user._id.toString() !== req.user._id.toString() && !req.user.isAdmin) { res.status(403); throw new Error('Not authorized to view this order'); }

issue: updateOrderToPaid does not verify order ownership — any authenticated user can mark any order as paid
evidence: const order = await Order.findById(req.params.id); order.isPaid = true; — no check that req.user._id matches order.user
recommendation: Add ownership check: verify req.user._id.toString() === order.user.toString() or that req.user.isAdmin before allowing payment status change.

issue: Hardcoded n8n admin credentials in docker-compose.yml committed to git
recommendation: Move all credentials to a .env file (not committed to git). Use docker-compose env_file directive or variable substitution (${N8N_PASSWORD}). Rotate the exposed values.

issue: Hardcoded shared secret 'proshop-secret' committed to git in n8n workflow JSON
evidence: "rightValue": "proshop-secret" — appears 4 times in wf1-manual-toggle.json and 2 times in wf2-scheduled-monitor.json
recommendation: Move secret to n8n environment variable / credential store. Replace hardcoded value with {{$env.AUTH_SECRET}} in the workflow. Rotate the secret since it is in git history.

issue: Hardcoded default authentication secret 'proshop-secret' in MCP REST API server
evidence: AUTH_SECRET = os.environ.get('MCP_AUTH_SECRET', 'proshop-secret') — if MCP_AUTH_SECRET env var is not set, the default 'proshop-secret' is used
recommendation: Remove the default value. Fail startup if MCP_AUTH_SECRET is not set: AUTH_SECRET = os.environ.get('MCP_AUTH_SECRET'); if not AUTH_SECRET: raise RuntimeError('MCP_AUTH_SECRET must be set'). Use a cryptographically random secret.

issue: JWT_SECRET set to trivial value 'abc123' in .env
evidence: JWT_SECRET = abc123 — this is the signing key for all JWTs; easily guessable
recommendation: Generate a strong random secret: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(64).toString('hex'))" and set it as JWT_SECRET.

issue: JWT_SECRET example value 'abc123' may be used in production by developers who copy .env.example to .env
evidence: JWT_SECRET = abc123 — the example file contains the same weak value as .env

issue: MongoDB $regex query built from unsanitized user input (keyword parameter) — potential ReDoS / regex injection
evidence: name: { $regex: req.query.keyword, $options: 'i' } — user input passed directly to $regex without escaping
recommendation: Escape regex metacharacters before passing to $regex: const escapeRegex = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'); then use { $regex: escapeRegex(req.query.keyword) }

issue: No rate limiting on login endpoint POST /api/users/login — vulnerable to brute-force attacks
evidence: router.post('/login', authUser) — no express-rate-limit or similar middleware
recommendation: Add express-rate-limit: import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit'; const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15*60*1000, max: 5 }); router.post('/login', loginLimiter, authUser)

issue: No rate limiting on registration endpoint POST /api/users — allows automated account creation
recommendation: Apply rate limiting to the registration endpoint: const registerLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60*60*1000, max: 5 }); router.route('/').post(registerLimiter, registerUser)

issue: No security headers middleware (helmet) — missing X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, etc.
evidence: No helmet import or manual security headers anywhere in server.js or middleware/
recommendation: Install and configure helmet: npm install helmet; import helmet from 'helmet'; app.use(helmet());

issue: No CORS configuration — default Express behavior allows all origins or relies on same-origin proxy
evidence: No cors middleware import or configuration in server.js
recommendation: Install and configure cors with explicit origin allowlist: npm install cors; import cors from 'cors'; app.use(cors({ origin: allowedOrigins, credentials: true }))

issue: Stack traces exposed in non-production error responses
evidence: stack: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? null : err.stack — correct guard exists, but development mode leaks stack traces
recommendation: Acceptable for development. Ensure NODE_ENV=production is always set in deployed environments. Consider logging stack traces server-side only instead of sending them in responses.

issue: JWT token expiry is 30 days — excessively long token lifetime increases exposure window if stolen
evidence: expiresIn: '30d' — 30-day expiry with no refresh token mechanism and no server-side revocation
recommendation: Implement short-lived access tokens (15-30 min) with HttpOnly refresh tokens. At minimum, reduce to 1-2 hours for access tokens.

issue: JWT token stored in localStorage — vulnerable to XSS token theft
evidence: localStorage.setItem('userInfo', JSON.stringify(data)) — token persisted in localStorage, accessible to any JS including XSS payloads
recommendation: Store tokens in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies instead of localStorage. This is documented in ADR-003 as accepted technical debt.

issue: isAdmin check uses stale JWT claim — demoted admins retain admin privileges until token expires (up to 30 days)
evidence: const admin = (req, res, next) => { if (req.user && req.user.isAdmin) { next() } — req.user.isAdmin comes from JWT decoded payload, not a fresh DB lookup
recommendation: For admin-required endpoints, perform a fresh DB lookup: const user = await User.findById(req.user._id); if (!user || !user.isAdmin) { return res.status(403).json({message: 'Not admin'}) }. This is documented in ADR-003 as a known gap.

issue: Seed data uses weak default password '123456' for all users including admin
evidence: password: bcrypt.hashSync('123456', 10) — trivially guessable password for admin@example.com
recommendation: Use stronger default passwords in seed data or generate random ones printed to console. Add password complexity validation in the registration endpoint.
